prompts: Write the scene that happens five minutes after something life-changing, not the moment itself.
Someone keeps a message unsent for years. Tonight, they finally delete it.
Two people share a secret they’ve never named out loud.
A character realizes they feel safe for the first time,for a stupid, tiny reason.
Write a conversation where no one says what they actually mean.
A character returns to a place they swore they’d never go back to.
Someone notices a small habit they picked up from a person who’s gone.
A love story told entirely through things left behind.
Write the moment a character stops waiting.
Someone hears their name spoken by the wrong person.
Write a character explaining something they’re embarrassed to care about.
A character talks to someone who isn’t listening anymore.
Write the internal monologue during an awkward silence.
Someone confesses something by accident.
Write the things a character doesn’t say during an argument.
A character narrates a mundane task while avoiding a difficult thought.
Someone practices a conversation that never actually happens.
A character realizes they miss a version of themselves.
Write about the moment something stops hurting as much.
Someone is afraid they’re too much, and then finds out they’re not.
A character chooses honesty even though it costs them.
Write the scene where a character finally asks for help.
Someone notices they’re no longer angry,just tired.
A character lets go of a future they’d been clinging to.
A place remembers everyone who’s loved there.
Time pauses for everyone except one person.
A character can revisit memories, but only the painful ones.
Someone keeps meeting the same person in different lives.
A message appears exactly when it’s needed.
A door only opens when someone is ready to leave.
Two people almost say “I love you” and don’t.
Write the moment a relationship changes direction.
Someone realizes they’ve been misreading another person entirely.
A character chooses to stay when it would be easier to leave.
Write a reunion that isn’t what either person expected.
A goodbye that feels unfinished.
“I didn’t think it would hurt like this.” Keep going.
“We promised not to talk about it.” Keep going.
“This wasn’t how I imagined seeing you again.” Keep going.
“I almost didn’t recognize myself.” Keep going.
“I should have left earlier.” Keep going.
“You don’t get to apologize like that.” Keep going.
“I kept the thing you told me to throw away.” Keep going.
